articles.title: Dólar hoje: BC vende US$ 1 bilhão mas moeda sobe para R$ 5,93 | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao oferecer dólares ao mercado, o BC aumentou a quantidade de moeda americana para tentar conter a alta. O impacto foi imediato, mas durou pouco. Economistas veem razões externas e principalmente internas para a disparada do dólar.
articles.summary: Dólar hoje atinge R$ 5,93 e sobe pelo 6º dia seguido, apesar de leilão de US$ 1 bilhão do Banco Central
articles.body:
O Banco Central fez, nesta quinta-feira (19), um leilão extraordinário de US$ 1 bilhão à vista no mercado de câmbio. Mesmo assim, a moeda americana subiu pelo sexto pregão seguido.

Quando o Banco Central entra em campo no câmbio é porque algum movimento atípico está acontecendo. Com muitas pessoas e empresas trocando reais pela segurança do dólar, a cotação da moeda americana passou dos R$ 5,90 ainda pela manhã. E aí, em um leilão não programado, o Banco Central vendeu US$ 1 bilhão - quase R$ 6 bilhões - das reservas internacionais brasileiras.

Ao oferecer dólares ao mercado, o BC aumentou a quantidade de moeda americana para tentar conter a alta. O impacto foi imediato. A cotação caiu por volta de meio-dia - o horário do leilão. Mas durou pouco. Alguns minutos depois, o dólar já subiu novamente. Fechou o dia em R$ 5,93, o maior valor desde 8 de abril de 2025.

Na quarta-feira (18), o Banco Central já havia oferecido US$ 1 bilhão em um outro tipo de leilão, o chamado “leilão de linha”. Nesse caso, funciona como um empréstimo: o BC vende dólares com o compromisso de recomprar em uma data já definida, evitando, assim, a queima de reservas internacionais.

Banco Central leiloa US$ 1 bilhão das reservas internacionais brasileiras, mas moeda americana sobe pelo sexto pregão seguido — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Os economistas veem razões externas e principalmente internas para a disparada do dólar.

“Existe uma parte que não podemos ignorar de jeito nenhum, que tem a ver com títulos norte-americanos. A gente teve recentemente alta até dos juros no Japão, o que também gerou pressão sobre a moeda brasileira. Mas eu daria um peso maior, nesse momento, à dinâmica doméstica, especialmente à discussão fiscal e também do próximo ministro da Fazenda”, diz André Perfeito, economista-chefe da Garantia Capital.

As incertezas com o rumo da economia continuam afetando a bolsa brasileira, que, nesta quinta-feira (19), caiu 0,69%. Os juros futuros subiram mais uma vez, com investidores exigindo taxas mais altas para emprestar dinheiro em um clima de incerteza e insatisfação com o plano de ajuste fiscal que o governo apresentou.

“Você tem alguns cortes de gastos que o mercado vai entender como insuficientes porque ele não resolve gastos, de fato, mas sim tenta atacar via arrecadação e criar também, simultaneamente, alguns gatilhos, o que não é suficiente no sentido de um corte mais permanente das despesas no Brasil. São questões que se somaram e fizeram esse movimento muito forte na moeda norte-americana”, afirma André Perfeito.

“O que preocupa mais o mercado, hoje, é a falta de um horizonte para estabilização da relação dívida sobre Produto Interno Bruto, a dívida/PIB. Quais serão os nomes da equipe econômica? Tudo isso importa para que a gente consiga tirar um pouco de pressão do dólar, dos juros e da bolsa também”, opina Felipe Salto, economista-chefe da Warren Investimentos.

articles.title: Macaé amplia emissão de carteira para autistas e cuidadores | G1
articles.standfirst: Cartão da Mãe Atípica começou a ser emitido pelo Detran-RJ nesta semana; em Macaé, pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista podem solicitar gratuitamente a CIPTEA pela internet.
articles.summary: Cartão da Mãe Atípica começou a ser emitido pelo Detran-RJ nesta semana; em Macaé, pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista podem solicitar gratuitamente a CIPTEA pela internet.
articles.body:
Pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) em Macaé podem solicitar gratuitamente, pela internet, a Carteira de Identificação da Pessoa com TEA (CIPTEA), documento que facilita o acesso a direitos como o atendimento prioritário.

O tema ganhou ainda mais relevância nesta semana com o início da emissão, pelo Detran-RJ, do Cartão da Mãe Atípica, voltado a mães, pais e responsáveis legais que atuam como principais cuidadores de pessoas com deficiência, transtornos do neurodesenvolvimento ou doenças raras.

Embora possam ser complementares, os documentos têm funções diferentes. O cartão estadual identifica o cuidador, enquanto a CIPTEA identifica a própria pessoa autista e auxilia na garantia de direitos previstos em lei, como o atendimento prioritário.

Macaé amplia acesso à CIPTEA; Estado passa a emitir cartão para mães atípicas — Foto: CIPTEA

Fernando, de 9 anos, sabe exatamente para que serve a carteira que usa no pescoço. “Para saber que eu sou autista”, diz o menino.

A avó dele, Michele Silva Pinto, afirma que a família pretende utilizar o sistema on-line para renovar o documento, que vence em 2028. Segundo ela, a possibilidade de fazer o pedido pela internet facilita a rotina dos responsáveis.

“Vai ajudar aquela mãe que não tem com quem deixar a criança. Pela internet, ela ganha tempo porque consegue fazer a solicitação de casa, do trabalho e até na sala de espera de uma terapia”, relata Michele.

Em Macaé, a CIPTEA pode ser solicitada pelo portal ciptea.macae.rj.gov.br , por celular ou computador. O usuário preenche os dados, envia a documentação exigida e acompanha a análise do pedido pela plataforma. Após a aprovação, a versão digital fica disponível para download no próprio sistema. Quem optar pelo documento físico também pode fazer a solicitação on-line e seguir as orientações para retirada.

O serviço é gratuito e oferecido pela Secretaria Municipal de Desenvolvimento Social, Direitos Humanos, Acessibilidade e Economia Solidária em parceria com a Secretaria Municipal de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação. Agora, todas as etapas da solicitação são realizadas pelo portal, sem necessidade de envio por e-mail.

A CIPTEA tem validade em todo o território nacional e facilita o acesso a direitos, como o atendimento prioritário em serviços públicos e privados. Em Macaé, o documento foi instituído pelo Decreto Municipal nº 007/2020, conforme a Lei Federal nº 13.977/2020, conhecida como Lei Romeo Mion.

Acesse ciptea.macae.rj.gov.br , preencha os dados solicitados, envie a documentação necessária e acompanhe o andamento do pedido pela plataforma. Após a aprovação, a versão digital fica disponível para download.

Carteira identifica pessoas com autismo e facilita atendimento prioritário; novo documento estadual é voltado a cuidadores. — Foto: CIPTEA

articles.title: Forget Apple. Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Is Pouring Nearly $1 Billion Into This Little-Known Tech Stock.
articles.summary: Berskhire Hathaway's only new stock last quarter was Bending Spoons, and it has put about $930 million into the little-known tech company ahead of its Q3 ear...
articles.body:
On Nov. 16, Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) (BRK.B) filed its quarterly 13F. A 13F is a report that shows which stocks a big investor held at the end of the quarter. Only one new stock was added, and it was a tech company called Bending Spoons (BSP) that went public just months ago. Former CEO Warren Buffett avoided tech stocks for years, so Berkshire adding BSP stock is an interesting shift now that Greg Abel is CEO. Berkshire's biggest tech bet has long been Apple (AAPL). It has sold about three-quarters of its AAPL stock from the peak, though Apple is still one of its largest holdings. The filing shows the July stake in Bending Spoons, while the second purchase came in October, after the quarter ended.

Berkshire bought shares in Bending Spoons when it first listed on the stock market in July, putting in $600 million. Then, in mid-October, Berkshire bought directly from the company instead of through the open market. It paid $33 per share for 10 million new shares, which is $330 million. In total, Berkshire has now put in about $930 million and owns about 4% of the company. The market read Berkshire buying a second time as strong confidence in Bending Spoons and not just testing the waters. BSP stock jumped on the news but has now cooled to just under $44 but is still well above the $33 Berkshire paid.

Bending Spoons is a technology company that acquires established digital businesses and works to make them more efficient and profitable. Berkshire Hathaway is among its backers. Its portfolio includes well-known names like AOL, Vimeo, Evernote, WeTransfer, and Airtable, along with apps like Remini and pet tracker Tractive. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in Milan, Italy, and is led by co-founder and CEO Luca Ferrari.

Since going public on July 1, BSP stock is up just over 7%, beating the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF's (IGV) roughly 2% increase in the same period and an 8% year-to-date (YTD) decline. The stock hit a record high of $59.50 on Oct. 15 after Berkshire added a $330 million investment. But much of that rally has since faded on profit-taking and broader software weakness, leaving the stock just under $44.

articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin release 'peace declaration' from unprecedented summit
articles.summary: By Jarrett Renshaw, Trevor Hunnicutt and Steve Holland SHENZHEN, China/WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - China, the United States and Russia agreed on a symboli...
articles.body:
By Jarrett Renshaw, Trevor Hunnicutt and Steve Holland

SHENZHEN, China/WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - China, the United States and Russia agreed on a symbolic "peace declaration" at an unprecedented three-way summit on Thursday and reaffirmed that nuclear war should never be fought, but announced no plans for arms control talks long sought by Trump.

A joint declaration released by Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin capped a three-day diplomatic swing by Trump through Asia that produced ‌few tangible victories, despite his repeated boasts about making history and brokering peace.

Instead, the trip raised fresh questions among US allies about his increasingly close relationships with Xi and with Putin, who continues to wage war against Ukraine.

Trump greeted Putin as "my friend" and received ‌a hug from Xi in the latest of the diplomatic spectacles he favors.

Those meetings, which have included discussions with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and summits with Putin, have drawn praise from some for his willingness to engage directly with US adversaries and criticism from others for giving autocrats a global stage.

The leaders pledged to advance reforms of the ​United Nations, to increase supplies of fuel products for all countries and to uphold the immunity enjoyed by state officials in international courts.

The declaration did not mention Russia's war in Ukraine or the US conflict with Iran, and in a press conference afterwards, Putin acknowledged it did not set ambitious goals and added that nobody would be forced to comply with its decisions.

The powers "reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought" and added that they would "conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation of nuclear weapons," without giving a time frame.

But the statement made no mention of negotiations on a trilateral nuclear arms reduction treaty, something Trump has pushed since his first term and that China has consistently rejected, arguing that its arsenal is much smaller than those of the other powers.

Trump referred to nuclear weapons at the start of the meeting, saying: "It's not an easy thing to ‌do – give them up."

He told NBC afterwards that it "went great."

"On a scale of zero to 10, ⁠I think it was a 12," he said. "Fantastic relationships built."

In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump said he would hold a news conference in Washington at noon (1700 GMT) on Friday.

China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said the countries would maintain coordination at working level after the "peace summit."
authors: By Jarrett Renshaw, Trevor Hunnicutt and Steve Holland

articles.title: Anthropic IPO sets retail trading record as market sell-off weighs on buying
articles.summary: Retail traders aggressively bought and sold shares during Anthropic's IPO.
articles.body:
Anthropic's ( ANT ) stock churned out more retail trading activity on its public debut than any other stock in its listing day going back to 2012, according to full Thursday trading data from Vanda Research.

The firm's data shows everyday investors traded $772 million worth of Anthropic shares, exceeding the $669 million recorded during SpaceX's ( SPCX ) first trading session in June and setting a record in Vanda's data, which goes back to 2012.

However, everyday investors were far less aggressive net buyers of shares through the day compared to SpaceX's blockbuster June listing. Net retail purchases totaled just $60 million or roughly half the $118 million that retail investors poured into SpaceX on its first day and a third less than the $92 million in Coinbase Global's ( COIN ) April 2021 debut, according to Vanda.

"Retail are turning up to trade Anthropic ... but not in the way that much of the street, ourselves included, had probably anticipated," Vanda Research analyst Viraj Patel wrote, noting that the share of retail buyers steadily declined across early trading.

Among the major reasons for the lower net buying, Patel cited "broader risk aversion in global markets" as major stock indexes fell Thursday. Smaller investors also may appear to be favoring an alternative to traditional stock trading, specifically the use of a crypto-related derivative product known as perpetual futures, which are tied to the price of the stock, Patel added.

The divergence suggests that retail investors were actively buying and selling Anthropic shares rather than accumulating them as aggressively as they did SpaceX. The net buying was also far below Vanda's estimate made ahead of the listing based on perpetual futures pricing .

The broader selloff came as retail investors have sold single stocks to fund their Anthropic purchases, rotating out of AI names like AMD ( AMD ) as buying in Nvidia ( NVDA ) stalled. Shares of AMD and Nvidia dropped 7% and 2%, respectively, in afternoon trading.

The final word on retail enthusiasm for the stock is still far from out, according to Patel. SpaceX's first-day net buying accounted for just 29% of its total in the first week, according to the company.

articles.title: Pedro Sánchez saca pecho del crecimiento y responde las preguntas de Feijóo: "España es un éxito de país"
articles.standfirst: El presidente defiende el avance económico y social frente a las críticas de la oposición
articles.summary: El presidente defiende el avance económico y social frente a las críticas de la oposición
articles.body: La televisión española se paralizaba este jueves 19 de noviembre para acoger el gran acontecimiento informativo de la campaña hacia el 29-N. Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo protagonizaban a partir de las 22:00 horas el esperado cara a cara organizado por la Academia de Televisión en Tres Cantos. En el intercambio sobre la situación económica, el debate se articuló en torno a la presión fiscal, la evolución de los precios, la corrupción y el rumbo de las políticas públicas. Frente a las preguntas sobre impuestos, cesta de la compra y pensiones, el presidente del Gobierno defendió la solidez de su gestión y el respaldo de las previsiones internacionales. Al abordar la coyuntura exterior y el panorama económico, Sánchez sostuvo: "Yo creo que esta semana la Comisión Europea nos ha dado una muy buena noticia". Según explicó, el organismo comunitario situó a España en cabeza entre los grandes socios europeos: "Ha dicho que España va a ser de nuevo este año la gran economía europea que más crezca, un 2,6 % del producto interior bruto en el año 2026". El presidente vinculó esa expansión con la creación de empleo y el mercado laboral, señalando que España aspira a ser "también la gran economía que más empleo cree". En ese sentido, recordó los registros de afiliación, los avances en participación laboral femenina y el colectivo de trabajadores por cuenta propia. Para resumir el balance de sus políticas en un contexto complejo, afirmó: "Esto lo que significa, en un tiempo tan turbulento como el que vivimos, que el modelo español funciona y que la vía socialdemócrata funciona". Añadió además que se ha compatibilizado el crecimiento y la reducción de emisiones con el refuerzo del Estado del bienestar, el aumento del salario mínimo interprofesional hasta el 75 %, la revalorización de las pensiones, el crecimiento de su hucha y la consolidación de las cuentas públicas con menos déficit y deuda. En el cierre de su intervención, atribuyó los resultados al conjunto de la sociedad y llamó a mantener el rumbo actual. "Todo ello es un éxito de país", aseguró antes de advertir de que "hay que perseverar en este avance, no dar un giro en política económica de 180 grados, lo que proponen el señor Feijóo y el señor Abascal, y continuar con este avance porque efectivamente los datos están ahí: la Comisión Europea ha dicho que España va a ser la gran economía europea que más crezca y más empleo cree".

articles.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
articles.summary: US House committee releases chip export data amid scrutiny of former Nvidia CEO’s alleged links to a Chinese spy.
articles.body:
The administration of United States President Donald Trump approved exports of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee has said.

The Department of Commerce’s approvals covered exports of 879,000 chips, including 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD, the committee said on Thursday.

Companies had sought permission to ship 3.4 million of them to China during the period, committee documents show.

The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the Trump administration faces heightened scrutiny following revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy , which fuelled renewed calls for a tougher stance against Chinese technology threats.

All four of the Chinese companies highlighted in the committee report are on the Pentagon’s list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.

The committee chair, Brian Mast, has “exercised his authorities under the Export Control Reform Act to publicly reveal export control license application information regarding NVIDIA and AMD’s AI chip licenses for the People’s Republic of China”, the committee said in a statement. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of the chips, which included Nvidia’s H200 and AMD’s equivalent MI325X.

News surrounding Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialling up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech threats.

“The fact that over 30 percent of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese military companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses,” said Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle.

Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were “subject to strict conditions and limited volumes”. It added that “despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China”.

AMD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Former US President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China’s military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence.

But Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum.

Nvidia’s stock ended the day down 3.3 percent, while AMD slumped 7.7 percent and the broader Nasdaq and S&P 500 were down 2.2 percent and 1.8 percent, respectively.

articles.title: NYC Lawmakers Weigh Overhaul of Amazon Delivery Worker Bill
articles.summary: New York City lawmakers are in discussions to modify a mandate that would require Amazon.com Inc. to directly hire thousands of delivery workers under a bill...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- New York City lawmakers are in discussions to modify a mandate that would require Amazon.com Inc. to directly hire thousands of delivery workers under a bill that has pitted the company against Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

The lawmakers are considering replacing the direct hire mandate with a menu of options, allowing Amazon to either directly employ the workers, use carriers like UPS or the US Postal Service, or contract with fully independent third-party operators, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

For the delivery companies, it would require a complete change from their current operating model, one of the people said. Amazon would have to give up oversight of the contracted companies, including control of their routes, daily delivery quotas, hiring, firing and disciplining employees, the people said.

The proposed revisions would represent a compromise on legislation that sought to reshape the delivery industry by requiring companies such as Amazon to bring workers employed by subcontractors onto their own payrolls. Under the changes being considered, Amazon could continue using its network of small business delivery partners but would have to grant them autonomy and come under greater city oversight of those relationships.

If an agreement is reached, the legislation could come up for a vote within a few weeks, according to the people.

"We've made clear we're willing to work with anyone who wants to make progress on this matter," said Amazon spokesperson Steve Kelly. "We appreciate that Speaker Julie Menin has met with numerous stakeholders on this bill, including us, and we'll remain engaged with her and her team as work on the bill continues to try and reach the best outcome for New Yorkers."

In a statement, a Menin spokesperson, Jack Lobel, said her office is "working around the clock with the bill sponsor and stakeholders to achieve legislation that protects workers, jobs, and street safety. A range of options are still on the table."

The bill, called the Delivery Protection Act, has gained the backing of an overwhelming majority of City Council members and Mamdani.

Initially, Amazon and the small business owners presented a united front against the bill. Amazon bankrolled a lobbying group that included many of its delivery partners, which also opposed the legislation.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos says 2 policies drive up housing costs, and it's 'not hard to figure out'
articles.summary: The Amazon founder says the causes of sky-high home prices are simpler than politicians make them sound.
articles.body:
House hunters have plenty of suspects for the price tags they're seeing on listing sites. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos thinks the case is already closed.

Bezos has been making the same argument since at least May. In November, he took it to Silicon Valley.

"If you want to know why housing is expensive, it's not very hard to figure out," Bezos said on Nov. 17 at Semafor's Silicon Valley & the World conference in Menlo Park, California. "We subsidize demand and constrain supply."

"If you have policies that do those two things, prices will grow, and things will get expensive," he said.

Bezos says these 2 levers keep home prices high

Bezos has already spelled out what he means by each half of that equation.

"We subsidize demand with things like tax policy, which is fine, but at the same time, we constrain supply," he said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on May 20. "We constrain supply with things like zoning and permitting."

Put simply, government makes it easier to buy a home while also making it harder to build one. More buyers chasing the same number of houses pushes prices up.

He also has a city he holds up as proof. "If you can look at a counterexample, which is Austin, where over the last 10 years they've implemented many policies designed to make it easier to build houses, and they have housing prices going down in Austin," Bezos said on Fox News' "Special Report" on Oct. 7.

The pressure shows up in household budgets. A family needed $120,800 a year to afford payments on a median-priced home at the end of 2025, up from $68,700 in 2020, according to Harvard University's Joint Center for Housing Studies .

Borrowing hasn't gotten any cheaper, either. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.11% as of Nov. 12, compared with 6.24% a year earlier, according to Freddie Mac .

That math is pushing more would-be buyers toward renting, with the income needed to buy a home now far above what it takes to lease one . Even with home prices slipping for several weeks in a row , affordability is still a long way from where buyers want it.

articles.title: Almost all of Anthropic’s employees are now millionaires
articles.summary: Anthropic’s stock market debut turned the vast majority of the young startup’s staff into overnight millionaires — some many times over.
articles.body:
Anthropic's stock market debut turned the vast majority of the young startup's staff into overnight millionaires — some many times over.

The company's headcount stood at 5,300 as of September this year, according to regulatory filings. After Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, about 600 employees entered the rarefied "centi-millionaire" club, with equity holdings valued north of $100 million, according to data from Hill.com , which tracks private-company shares.

As many as 2,800 staffers, known internally as "Ants," have holdings valued above $10 million. And about 5,100 — 96% of the staff — are sitting on equity north of $1 million.

"What's most surprising here is how quickly this this happened," Andrew Benson, Hill's founder and CEO, told CNN on Thursday, noting Anthropic has seen very little attrition. "It's been pretty clear for some time that Anthropic is a rocket ship, and so it definitely discouraged people from leaving because they knew what the opportunity cost of that would be."

It's not unusual for Silicon Valley startups, which are typically light on cash, to pay their staff with a combination of salary and stock. The promise of a future acquisition or initial public offering tends to keep workers motivated to work hard and stick it out until payday.

But few startups have grown as big or as quickly as Anthropic. The company, founded in 2021, had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024.

As with most tech startups, Benson noted, "being early is more important, in terms of a financial outcome, than being senior … You could be very low on the totem pole, and if you joined in 2023 or 2024, you're likely to have a significantly better outcome than a senior person who joined earlier this year."

SpaceX, by contrast, spent more than two decades as a private company before its blockbuster IPO in June. That debut minted around 4,400 millionaires, out of a staff of 22,000.

Anthropic's IPO is also unique for allowing non-founder insiders to cash out on Day One of trading. In most IPOs, staff are subject to a "lockup" period — typically three to six months — during which they can't sell their shares. But Anthropic's listing included a complex, staggered lockup schedule that allowed non-founder insiders to cash out up to 10% of their shares as soon as the stock began trading. (It's not known how many insiders may have taken advantage of the opportunity Thursday.)

And unlike SpaceX, which has employees spread across Texas, California and Florida, Anthropic is uniquely concentrated in San Francisco, a city whose entire economy has been reshaped by sudden surges of tech wealth.

articles.summary: By Deborah Mary Sophia Nov 19 (Reuters) - Criminal duo Lucia and Jason's blitz through Vice City in "GTA VI" is set to help Take-Two Interactive, the publish...
articles.body:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Criminal duo Lucia and Jason's blitz through Vice City in "GTA VI" is set to help Take-Two Interactive, the publisher of the blockbuster game that is ‌now a global cultural phenomenon, rake in more than $2 billion in estimated first-day sales.

Take-Two Interactive ( TTWO ), the ‌parent company of GTA developer Rockstar Games, is not a household name despite its portfolio of massive hits including the "Red Dead Redemption" ​franchise and the "NBA 2K" basketball series.

Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates total units sold at 24.58 million, as of Thursday evening, translating to about $2.36 billion in revenue for Take-Two. That is almost three times the roughly $800 million worth of copies GTA V sold on its first day in 2013, widely regarded as the best-selling videogame in the first 24 ‌hours.

Meanwhile, Take-Two has remained tight-lipped about ⁠GTA VI demand since it opened for pre-orders in June, limiting commentary to saying demand has been "unprecedented" or "far exceeding expectations."

"The title is so widely anticipated, consumers appear very, very ⁠excited, and all the press so far has been universally positive, but we still aren't ready to declare victory," CEO Strauss Zelnick said on Take-Two's earnings call earlier this month.

"We tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs."

Take-Two ​has shelled out an estimated $1 billion or more in ​production costs for GTA VI, making it one ‌of the most expensive entertainment projects.

Sensor Tower estimates that the game's promotional trailer, GTA VI "Extended Look", on Netflix in August helped drive a sixfold jump in pre-orders.

In Miami, which Vice City is based on, the city's NBA team celebrated the release on Wednesday with a Vice City-themed match.

Over the weekend, the company is hosting "GTA VI: The Festival" - a music show with a star-studded line-up that includes Grammy-winning rapper Cardi B, hip hop record ‌producer Metro Boomin and rapper Travis Scott.

Investors have ​been waiting to hear from Take-Two about its plans for a ​PC launch of GTA VI and an ​online version rollout. The online, multiplayer component of a videogame is crucial in turning the ‌title into a recurring revenue engine.

Some industry ​analysts are expecting the PC ​launch and online mode in 2027.

Brokerage TD Cowen named Take-Two one of its 'Best Ideas' for 2027, with its analyst Doug Creutz upbeat about the company's financial prospects when the game releases online.

articles.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard hit by cyber incidents;  data of thousands of customers leaked
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed separate cyber incidents involving third-party service providers, with customer information, including
articles.body: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed separate cyber incidents involving third-party service providers, with customer information, including thousands of email addresses, exposed in data leaks. The breach at JPMorgan, the largest US lender, appears to have compromised marketing records containing customer names, email addresses and, in some cases, phone numbers and postal codes. All three companies said their payment systems were not affected and no card payment information was exposed.JPMorgan said on Thursday that attackers had targeted vendors providing services to the bank and accessed certain marketing data held by them. The bank said it was investigating the incident and would contact affected customers directly."Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses," a JPMorgan spokesperson said.The bank did not disclose the number of customers affected. The information exposed appears to involve only a small fraction of Chase's tens of millions of customers, according to the Associated Press.Hackers claim to have accessed thousands of JPMorgan recordsThe disclosure of leak follows claims by a cyber extortion group called "n0n", which said on November 16 that it had obtained cardmember engagement records from JPMorgan.A Reuters review of data posted by the group found more than 16,000 customer email addresses, some phone numbers and postal codes, as well as what appeared to be 124 bank employee email addresses.The bank clarified that the cyberattack was unrelated to service disruptions earlier this week, when a software bug affected transaction processing at JPMorgan and other banks."There is no connection to service disruption of some customers experienced earlier this week," the spokesperson said.Visa, Mastercard confirm separate vendor breachesThe same hacking group made claims involving Visa and Mastercard on November 16. Both companies confirmed incidents at third-party providers but said their payment networks and customers' ability to use their cards were unaffected.Visa said its incident involved a third-party service provider in the Asia-Pacific region. "Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected," a spokesperson said.Mastercard said a third-party breach exposed a limited number of email addresses belonging to cardholders enrolled in a specific benefits programme. It described the information as non-payment data and said there was no impact on its payment network."At this time, the exposure has been contained and our teams are working with the provider to support the impacted cardholders as needed," a Mastercard spokesperson said, according to AP.Data posted by the group found purported Visa customer records across several Asia-Pacific markets, including Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Singapore and Australia, as per Reuters. The Mastercard material appeared to contain marketing data related to customers in North America, the Middle East and Africa.The incidents have renewed questions about how much customer information financial companies share with external vendors and how closely they monitor the security of those providers."Customers don't distinguish between a bank and a vendor when it comes to a cyberattack, so there is a question of reputational risk here," said Carissa Robb of consulting firm SolomonEdwards.She said companies needed to face greater scrutiny over how frequently they review the data shared with vendors and whether all of it is necessary.The JPMorgan disclosure comes amid a series of technology disruptions affecting businesses and infrastructure providers. The bank's transaction-processing problems earlier this week also prompted inquiries from US banking regulators, who sought to assess the impact and establish whether the incident was cyber-related.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Master: relatório da PF sobre Mendonça cita tentativas de aproximação de Vorcaro ao ministro do STF | G1
articles.standfirst: André Mendonça, do STF, pediu a Fachin que dê 'ampla publicidade' ao relatório elaborado pela PF sobre menções ao ministro. Presidente da Corte atendeu ao pedido.
articles.summary: André Mendonça, do STF, pediu a Fachin que dê 'ampla publicidade' ao relatório elaborado pela PF sobre menções ao ministro. Presidente da Corte atendeu ao pedido.
articles.body:
O relatório da Polícia Federal com menções ao ministro André Mendonça , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), detalha tentativas de aproximação do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, e de pessoas próximas ao dono do Master, ao magistrado da Suprema Corte.

Nesta sexta-feira (20), Mendonça pediu à presidência do STF que retire o sigilo do relatório do documento produzido pela PF com menções a ele. Depois disso, o blog teve acesso ao conteúdo do relatório sobre Mendonça.

No documento, há um episódio, já conhecido, em que o advogado Ciro Soares relata, em fevereiro de 2025, a Daniel Vorcaro que estava levando o Mendonça para fazer um terno no estabelecimento de um alfaiate famoso.

Ciro Soares enviou um áudio ao ex-banqueiro em que, segundo a Polícia Federal , afirma:

"Fala, Vorcarinho... Trabalhando por você, levei o André lá no Vasco agora, pra fazer um terno". A mensagem é acompanhada de uma foto do advogado com Mendonça (veja na imagem abaixo).

Sobre este caso, o ministro do STF apresentou as notas fiscais demonstrando que foi ele quem pagou pelo trabalho de alfaiataria .

Advogado enviou áudio para Vorcaro em que relatava que, em fevereiro de 2025, levou André Mendonça para fazer um terno em uma alfaiataria — Foto: Reprodução

De acordo com a Polícia Federal, "não foram identificados, durante as buscas realizadas por palavras-chave, registros que evidenciem diálogo direto entre os interlocutores Daniel Vorcaro e o ministro André Mendonça , seja por meio de aplicativos de mensagens, seja por qualquer outro canal de comunicação observado".

No pedido de divulgação do relatório da PF encaminhado ao presidente do STF, Edson Fachin , nesta sexta, Mendonça afirma:

"Considerando que [o relatório] Pet nº 17.146 diz respeito exclusivamente à minha pessoa, registro que renuncio expressamente ao sigilo relacionado às informações ali contidas e, por conseguinte, solicito à Vossa Excelência que dê ampla publicidade à íntegra dos autos da Pet nº 17.146, franqueando o acesso aos autos a qualquer do povo".

Nesta semana, o presidente do STF enviou cópia dos relatórios produzidos pela PF sobre as relações do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro , ex-dono do Banco Master, aos ministros que foram citados no material.

Ao menos cinco ministros confirmaram que o material foi disponibilizado pela presidência do STF. Segundo esses relatos, os documentos só trazem citações a eles. Não há informações sobre colegas.

Ao todo, a PF entregou 10 relatórios a Fachin. Desses, seis já foram arquivados. O presidente do STF encaminhou à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) quatro "para exame e avaliação das providências que entender cabíveis" em 15 dias.

Caberá à PGR avaliar se o conteúdo justifica a abertura de uma apuração, se é preciso aprofundar os fatos narrados com novas diligências, se há dados para medidas mais gravosas, como uma denúncia, ou se é o caso de arquivamento.

Além disso, Fachin informou que as informações recebidas serão mantidas, no momento, em sigilo. Mendonça se antecipou e pediu a divulgação do documento que tem menções a ele.

O diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues, se reuniu na noite de quarta-feira (18) com Fachin para entregar os relatórios citando os ministros do tribunal mencionados ou que trocaram mensagens com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.

O material deve detalhar menções e citações aos ministros sem avançar sobre condutas criminosas ou não. Os documentos chegaram ao STF quando a primeira fase da Operação Compliance Zero , que investiga as fraudes do Master e suas conexões, completou um ano.

articles.title: Salário mínimo compra 23 kg de acém a menos do que em 2007: entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: País se tornou o maior produtor mundial em 2025, mas a carne disponível para os brasileiros diminuiu, com exportações em alta e renda que não acompanhou os preços.
articles.summary: País se tornou o maior produtor mundial em 2025, mas a carne disponível para os brasileiros diminuiu, com exportações em alta e renda que não acompanhou os preços.
articles.body:
Com um salário mínimo, um trabalhador brasileiro consegue comprar hoje cerca de 39 kg de acém , um dos cortes bovinos mais baratos do açougue. Há 19 anos, a mesma renda levava para casa quase 62 kg , segundo levantamento da economista Lygia Pimentel, CEO da consultoria Agrifatto.

É uma perda de mais de um terço do poder de compra em relação à carne.

O pior momento da série foi em 2021 , auge da pandemia de Covid-19, quando o salário mínimo comprava apenas 33,8 kg.

Nos anos seguintes, o indicador se recuperou e chegou a 45 kg em 2024, mas voltou a cair depois daquele ano. Veja o histórico abaixo.

Gráfico mostra o poder de compra de carne bovina no Brasil. — Foto: g1

A perda de poder de compra acontece em meio a um paradoxo. Em 2025, o Brasil produziu um volume recorde de carne bovina, 11,1 milhões de toneladas, e se tornou o maior produtor mundial, ultrapassando os Estados Unidos pela primeira vez em 60 anos . Ainda assim, a quantidade de carne disponível para os brasileiros diminuiu. (veja gráfico abaixo)

Duas forças explicam esse movimento: lá fora, a demanda aquecida levou o Brasil a exportar como nunca, mas aqui dentro, a renda das famílias não acompanhou a alta dos preços.

Levantamento do Rabobank também mostra a queda no consumo: de 43 kg por habitante ao ano em 2006, recorde histórico, para cerca de 32 kg em 2025.

“ A gente não vai voltar mais para os patamares de 43 quilos . Inevitavelmente, vamos ser preenchidos por proteínas mais baratas. [...] Vemos um esforço muito grande do setor suíno, transferindo cortes de boi que conhecemos bem, como a picanha e o filé, para o suíno, buscando dar mais atratividade no supermercado”, afirma Wagner Yanaguizawa, analista de proteínas do Rabobank.

Mesmo com a inflação oficial girando em torno de 4,5%, muitas famílias seguem com o orçamento apertado. Entre dívidas, juros altos e gastos essenciais, sobra menos dinheiro para itens como a carne bovina. É o que a economista Lygia Pimentel, CEO da Agrifatto, chama de “inflação silenciosa”.

“Em 2018, um salário mínimo chegou a comprar o equivalente a 2,18 cestas básicas por mês. Entre 2010 e 2019, a média era de 2,10 cestas. De 2022 para cá, ela caiu para cerca de 1,70”, afirma.

Comparação entre a inflação do acém e os reajustes do salário mínimo em janeiro de cada ano. — Foto: Arte/g1

O enfraquecimento do poder de compra tem funcionado inclusive como um freio para novas altas da carne no varejo, diz Fernando Henrique Iglesias, analista da Safras & Mercado.

“Os consumidores das classes C, D e E não conseguem absorver tantos reajustes . Quando os preços sobem, eles migram para proteínas mais baratas, como frango e carne suína, ou para cortes que pesam menos no orçamento. Para as classes A e B, isso não faz diferença. Elas continuam comendo carne bovina”, diz Iglesias.

Para Yanaguizawa, essa mudança tende a se aprofundar. “A carne bovina no Brasil está passando por um processo de virar um item de luxo para algumas classes econômicas, ficando reservada para ocasiões mais especiais”, afirma.

Dados levantados pela Agrifatto mostram que, enquanto a produção de carne bovina cresceu 7,2% em 2025, as exportações avançaram em um ritmo mais acelerado, com alta de quase 20%. Já a oferta para os brasileiros encolheu 0,5%.

O movimento não é inédito. A última vez que isso aconteceu foi em 2019, quando a peste suína africana dizimou parte do rebanho chinês e provocou uma disparada nas compras do país asiático. Desta vez, porém, a demanda vem de um número maior de países, já que grandes exportadores, como EUA, Austrália e Argentina, enfrentam dificuldades para ampliar a oferta.

Variação da oferta aos brasileiros e produção interna de carne bovina. — Foto: g1

Esse cenário fez crescer a parcela da produção destinada ao exterior. Historicamente, cerca de 70% da carne que o Brasil produz fica no mercado interno. Em 2025, essa fatia caiu para 61%, segundo levantamento do Rabobank.

Nos últimos anos, o Brasil passou a reunir uma combinação rara no mercado global de carne bovina: produção em expansão, preços competitivos e capacidade de fornecer grandes volumes de forma estável.

O recorde de produção não é um fenômeno pontual , mas resultado de uma mudança estrutural da pecuária brasileira. Investimentos em genética e tecnologia, como a expansão da inseminação artificial, aumentaram a produtividade dos rebanhos e permitiram que os animais chegassem mais cedo ao abate.

“Aconteceu que a gente ampliou a produção enquanto o resto do mundo encolheu. Foi um alinhamento de astros, uma feliz coincidência para o produtor brasileiro”, afirma Pimentel.

Com mais carne disponível no Brasil e menos nos países concorrentes, o produto brasileiro ficou ainda mais barato em comparação ao de outros exportadores. Normalmente, a carne brasileira custa cerca de 14% menos do que a média dos principais exportadores mundiais. Nos últimos dois anos, essa diferença chegou a 25%, segundo a Agrifatto.

“O Brasil estava muito competitivo e o mundo falou: vou buscar no Brasil. Batemos recorde de parceiros internacionais porque conseguimos oferecer um volume grande, estável e a um preço muito competitivo”, diz a economista.

Segundo o Ministério da Agricultura, o volume embarcado cresceu 20,4% em 2025 na comparação com 2024. Além de ampliar as vendas para mercados já consolidados, como China (+24,6%) e União Europeia (+57%), o Brasil ganhou espaço em países como Vietnã (+129%) e México (+157%), para onde os embarques mais que dobraram em volume. Para a Indonésia, o crescimento foi ainda maior: +276%.

Principais destinos da carne brasileira, em volume. — Foto: Arte/g1

A tendência é que o Brasil permaneça na liderança global nos próximos anos e que frigoríficos e produtores direcionem cada vez mais esforços para o mercado externo. Na comparação com outros grandes produtores, o país reúne hoje as melhores condições para ampliar a produção em larga escala e atender ao crescimento da demanda mundial.

“Os frigoríficos, em termos de estratégia, não vão pensar duas vezes em tirar carne do mercado local para mandar para fora, porque a rentabilidade do mercado externo é muito maior”, afirma Yanaguizawa.

Ele conta que a tonelada de carne vendida no Brasil gira em torno de R$ 30 mil, enquanto a mesma quantidade exportada atinge R$ 37 mil, uma rentabilidade entre 22% e 23% superior.

Mas a ideia de que exportar é “o melhor negócio” não é consenso . Para Pimentel, a decisão entre vender no mercado interno ou exportar está longe de ser simples.

“Essa conversa de que ‘é melhor exportar do que vender aqui dentro’ não é necessariamente verdade. Seria muito mais fácil para as indústrias venderem 100% no mercado doméstico, porque o mercado interno é muito mais estável.”

Segundo a economista, exportar remunera mais, mas também carrega riscos que fogem ao controle das empresas.

“O mercado externo é temperamental e volátil. Quando um governo decide suspender as compras por motivos políticos ou sanitários, o exportador fica com ‘o mico na mão’. Às vezes, a notícia de um bloqueio chega quando você já tem centenas de contêineres na água, navegando há 45 ou 60 dias pelo oceano, sem saber o que fazer com aquela carga.”

Pimentel cita restrições impostas recentemente por mercados importantes como exemplos de situações que podem afetar exportadores de uma hora para outra. Neste ano, a China passou a limitar as compras por meio de cotas de importação , e a União Europeia suspendeu a entrada de carne bovina brasileira de forma repentina, por uma divergência sanitária.

Ela ressalta ainda que exportar exige uma estrutura complexa e investimentos contínuos. Para acessar determinados mercados, os frigoríficos precisam adequar instalações às exigências sanitárias de cada país, manter equipes especializadas e desenvolver uma rede logística capaz de atender clientes ao redor do mundo.

Ainda assim, a tendência aponta para fora. A produção deve recuar em 2026, mas vai continuar acima do observado nos últimos anos: depois de décadas produzindo entre 7 milhões e 8 milhões de toneladas por ano, o Brasil passou a operar em um novo patamar de cerca de 10 milhões de toneladas .

Exportações e oferta interna também devem diminuir neste ano. Para Pimentel, porém, o principal recado de 2025 é que, mesmo em fases de produção menor, uma parcela maior da carne brasileira tende a ir para o exterior nos próximos anos.

Imagem de carne bovina. — Foto: Gabriel Zachl/pexels

articles.title: 'Não podíamos pagar uma casa para nossa família, então decidimos comprar uma junto com desconhecidos' | G1
articles.standfirst: Os altos preços dos imóveis fazem com que pessoas e famílias no Canadá que não conseguem comprar uma casa busquem se associar a desconhecidos que enfrentem a mesma situação.
articles.summary: Os altos preços dos imóveis fazem com que pessoas e famílias no Canadá que não conseguem comprar uma casa busquem se associar a desconhecidos que enfrentem a mesma situação.
articles.body:
A família Pullman, à esquerda, e a família Wilcox compraram uma casa juntas, pouco depois que se conheceram. — Foto: Elizabeth Wilcox/Arquivo pessoal via BBC

Elizabeth e Tom Wilcox subitamente perceberam que nunca conseguiriam comprar a casa que eles queriam, para o casal e seus dois filhos. Até que eles tomaram uma decisão inusitada.

Eles começaram a procurar outro casal com filhos pequenos , totalmente desconhecidos. Sua intenção era propor a compra de um imóvel em partes iguais, para que todos pudessem se mudar juntos.

Os Wilcox moram em Vancouver, no Canadá. E, há tempos, os custos de moradia na cidade estão entre os mais altos do país.

Eles estavam desesperados para comprar uma casa que tivesse um jardim nos fundos, onde seus filhos pudessem brincar.

"Queríamos uma casa com um quintal onde coubesse uma cama elástica, em um bairro onde pudéssemos caminhar, mas não tínhamos condições", contou Elizabeth Wilcox, chefe de projetos no setor de saúde.

Seu orçamento era de um milhão de dólares canadenses (cerca de US$ 700 mil, ou R$ 4 milhões). Este valor só permitia que eles procurassem um pequeno apartamento, na melhor das hipóteses com sacada.

Foi então que ela teve a ideia de comprar o imóvel em conjunto com outra família.

'Economizamos dezenas de milhares de dólares'

Os Wilcox publicaram um anúncio no boletim eletrônico de uma imobiliária local. Mas foram necessários dois anos para que eles, finalmente, conhecessem a família com a qual se associariam: Ashley Pullman, seu marido e seus dois filhos.

Em 2023, os Wilcox e os Pullman compraram em conjunto uma casa unifamiliar com seis dormitórios, mais um jardim nos fundos, por CAN$ 1,85 milhões (cerca de US$ 1,3 milhão, ou R$ 7,5 milhões, pelo câmbio atual).

As duas famílias dividiram a entrada de CAN$ 250 mil (US$ 175 mil, R$ 1 milhão) e continuam pagando em partes iguais as parcelas da hipoteca, que somam CAN$ 3,9 mil por mês (cerca de US$ 2,7 mil, ou R$ 15,8 mil).

Eles também dividem equitativamente as contas e outras despesas, como os reparos necessários na moradia.

Para Elizabeth Wilcox, o acordo fez com que as duas famílias economizassem "dezenas de milhares de dólares".

As mães Ashley Pullman (esq.) e Elizabeth Wilcox contam que as duas famílias se dão bem. — Foto: Elizabeth Wilcox via BBC

Não existem dados oficiais sobre o número de pessoas que compram moradias com pessoas que não conheciam anteriormente.

Parimal Gosai é o fundador e CEO (diretor-executivo) do aplicativo e website Husmates, que conecta pessoas que desejam comprar casas com desconhecidos em Toronto, a maior cidade do Canadá. Ele afirma ter observado forte aumento de interesse na cidade, em resposta aos altos preços dos imóveis.

Segundo Gosai, este pode ser considerado "um relacionamento financeiro, o que elimina o componente emocional".

Não se sabe ao certo até que ponto esta prática é comum em outras partes do mundo.

David Hollingworth, da agência hipotecária britânica L&C, acredita que também haja no Reino Unido pessoas que comprem imóveis em conjunto, embora não tenha presenciado nenhum caso pessoalmente. Mas é algo muito pouco frequente, segundo ele.

"Recordo que, antes da covid-19, houve um evento em um pub de Londres, como os que existem para formar casais, mas para pessoas que procuravam comprar casas com desconhecidos", ele conta. "Não sei até que ponto aquilo teve sucesso."

Os Wilcox e os Pullman juntaram recursos para comprar uma casa unifamiliar em Vancouver, no Canadá — Foto: Elizabeth Wilcox via BBC

Três anos se passaram e os Wilcox e os Pullman garantem que continuam mantendo boa convivência.

Cada família tem alguns espaços privados, como suas próprias cozinhas. Mas eles compartilham uma grande sala de estar no porão, que inclui uma academia em um dos cantos e um congelador compartilhado.

"Quando alguém diz que irá ao porão fazer exercício, sabemos que não devemos entrar por um momento", conta Elizabeth Wilcox. "E nunca houve nenhum problema."

Ashley Pullman concorda que não há desentendimentos entre as duas famílias.

"Pode ser arrogância, mas meu marido e eu achávamos que éramos o tipo de pessoas que conseguiria conviver com desconhecidos", afirma ela.

A consultora de negócios independente de Toronto Sabrina Bowman é coproprietária de uma residência com duas outras pessoas, desde 2018.

Quando assinou o contrato e se mudou, Bowman não conhecia um dos outros dois coproprietários.

Ela não se sente à vontade para divulgar os detalhes financeiros, mas conta que eles decidiram dividir o depósito e as parcelas da hipoteca em função da renda de cada um.

Bowman acredita que é possível resolver eventuais desentendimentos domésticos a tempo com conversas abertas.

"Para nós, o importante é contar com mecanismos para nos comunicarmos sobre tudo o que acontece em casa", explica ela.

Eles têm reuniões periódicas para discutir as tarefas domésticas, temas financeiros, comemorações de aniversário e possíveis desentendimentos.

"É excelente observar as pessoas sendo honestas sobre algo que talvez as incomode e poder encontrar uma solução", conta Bowman.

Sabrina Bowman acredita ser importante manter comunicação aberta entre os coproprietários. — Foto: Sabrina Bowman via BBC

Tanto na casa de Sabrina Bowman em Toronto, quanto no lar dos Wilcox e dos Pullman em Vancouver, existem contratos legais para o caso de alguém desejar vender o imóvel e se mudar.

Nas duas moradias, são especificados prazos razoáveis de aviso prévio. No caso de Toronto, o comprador que decidir se mudar é obrigado a oferecer primeiramente aos que ficarem a oportunidade de comprar sua parte.

A advogada imobiliária Tanya Walker, de Toronto, destaca que estas garantias legais são fundamentais.

"É preciso ter algo que vincule legalmente os moradores em vez de uma porção de correios eletrônicos e mensagens no Facebook que podem ser muito difíceis de reunir no caso de uma eventual disputa", explica ela.

Em Vancouver, Elizabeth Wilcox afirma que nenhuma das duas famílias determinou por quanto tempo irão morar naquela casa.

"Todos nós estamos muito satisfeitos com a distribuição e a localização, de forma que seria difícil nos mudarmos", ela conta.

"Não consigo expressar com palavras a emoção que senti ao ver as crianças pularem na cama elástica pela primeira vez ou correr em círculos pelo nosso pequeno gramado."

articles.summary: Wall Street took another hit on Thursday as the AI party appeared to be losing its fizz.
articles.body: Wall Street took another hit on Thursday as the AI party appeared to be losing its fizz. US stocks tumbled again as investors continued to dump AI-linked shares, questioning whether the technology's spectacular rally had finally run out of steam.Even Anthropic's blockbuster stock market debut, which saw its shares soar well above the expected price, failed to lift the mood, as worries over sky-high valuations, expensive borrowing and whether massive AI investments will pay off kept investors on edge.The S&P500 fell 2%, marking its sixth straight day of losses. This is its longest losing streak in two and a half years. The index is now 8.2% below the record high it touched last month.The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points, or 2.3%. The sell-off was broad-based, with more than 90% of the stocks in the S&P500 ending the day lower.Anthropic's strong debut fails to lift moodThe market initially showed signs of recovery after Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, made its stock market debut on Thursday.The company priced its shares at $83 each, higher than its earlier expected range of $70 to $78. Soon after trading began on the Nasdaq shortly before noon, the shares climbed above $115.The strong debut briefly lifted the S&P500 by as much as 1.3%. However, the gains did not last. Anthropic shares eventually closed at $97.17, up 17.1% from their IPO price.The strong demand for the shares showed that investors were still interested in AI companies, despite the recent fall in their stock prices. However, the positive response to Anthropic's listing was not enough to stop the wider market decline.Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, described the current market conditions as “a very turbulent, white-knuckle period.”AI stocks give up early gains as selling returnsSeveral major AI-linked stocks started Thursday's session with gains but later slipped into losses.Micron Technology, which has benefited from rising demand for computer memory because of the AI boom, initially gained 7.8%. However, it reversed course and ended the day 2.1% lower.CoreWeave, which buys AI chips and rents access to them to customers through the cloud, also saw its shares swing sharply. After rising 10.5% in the morning, the stock ended the session down 6.1%.Nvidia shares followed a similar pattern. The stock erased its early gain of 4.7% and closed 3.3% lower as concerns about the AI industry continued to weigh on investors.AI bubble: Why investors are worriedThe recent fall in AI stocks comes amid growing concerns about whether their high prices can be justified.One of the biggest worries is that shares of AI companies may have become too expensive after their sharp rise. Investors are also questioning whether AI will generate enough profits and improve productivity enough to justify the huge amounts companies are spending on data centres.High interest rates have added to these concerns. With borrowing becoming more expensive, investors fear that companies may find it harder to raise the money needed to expand their AI businesses.Political developments have also added to the uncertainty. Sweeping victories for Democrats in the US midterm elections this month have raised concerns that AI companies could face more regulations.Another development adding to the concerns was the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang was one of the biggest supporters of the AI industry and helped build investor interest in the technology. He also used some of Nvidia's huge profits to support the industry's growth.In the bond market, US treasury yields declined as investors moved towards investments considered safer amid the fall in stock prices.The yield on the 10-year US Treasury slipped to 5.04% from 5.07% on Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, so when bond prices rise, their yields fall.Asian markets mixed, European stocks end lowerElsewhere, stock markets remained mixed.Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.7%, helped by a 4.6% gain in SoftBank Group. The company was an early investor in OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and a competitor to Anthropic.South Korea's Kospi also gained 1.4%, supported by a rise in stocks linked to the AI boom.However, stocks were weaker in other parts of Asia and Europe. Germany's DAX fell 1.1%.At the end of Thursday's trading session, the S&P 500 dropped 147.80 points to 7,175.83. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,101.11 points to close at 49,097.06, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points to 23,879.20.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Trump administration approved nearly 9 lakh Nvidia and AMD AI chips for Chinese firms
articles.summary: The US, under Donald Trump's administration, approved the shipment of 879,868 AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD to Chinese companies, which were identified
articles.body: The US, under Donald Trump's administration, approved the shipment of 879,868 AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD to Chinese companies, which were identified as military-linked by the US department of defense.According to newly released documents from the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the approvals included Nvidia's sensitive H200 chips and their AMD equivalent. The shipments were cleared through 21 licence applications as of May 11.Some of China's biggest companies featured on the recipient list. Tencent and its subsidiaries were approved to receive 1.5 lakh chips, followed by Alibaba with 75,000, Baidu with 43,000 and BYD with 4,000.All four companies are on the defense department's 2026 list of alleged Chinese military companies operating in the US.The disclosures were made possible by a provision under the Export Control Reform Act, which allowed Rep. Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, to release details of the licence applications.The committee said Mast exercised his legislative authority to “publicly reveal export control license application information” concerning Nvidia and AMD's AI chip licences for China.The revelations prompted criticism from Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), the committee's ranking member, who questioned the Trump administration's handling of chip export restrictions.Accusing the administration of mishandling export controls, Meeks said it “has put our national security and technology edge at risk.”He also questioned the Bureau of Industry and Security's enforcement of the rules, saying it had failed “to enforce the rules.” He added that “Congress must now conduct rigorous oversight of the administration’s policies.”Nvidia said the licensing process had involved a lengthy review and that the approvals came with restrictions.An Nvidia spokesperson told The Hill, “the review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes.”The company also clarified that receiving licences did not mean shipments were continuing. “Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China,” the spokesperson added.AMD also responded to the disclosures, saying it followed the applicable US export control requirements.“AMD complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations,” the company told The Hill in a statement.The latest disclosure comes amid earlier scrutiny of the Trump administration's decision to approve Nvidia's H200 chip sales last year.Mast had led House probes into the administration's approval of the shipments. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had previously argued before federal government officials that selling China the company's third- or fourth-best chips would make the country dependent on US-made infrastructure.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Up to 90% corpus withdrawal allowed in major PF reform
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) on Thursday decided to let retiring members opt for a systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) - giving
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) on Thursday decided to let retiring members opt for a systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) - giving them the opportunity to withdraw only a part of their corpus and earn interest on the remaining amount. Till now, members had to withdraw the entire corpus within three years of retirement.Separately, in case of partial withdrawals - a year after mandating that 25% of the corpus must be kept as minimum balance with EPFO - it decided to dilute the rule and allowed members to withdraw 90% of their corpus for three specified categories - essential needs (illness, education, marriage); housing needs; and special circumstances. Besides, it also slashed the waiting period in case of withdrawals made during the period of joblessness to two months, instead of 12 months earlier. "(EPFO) approved the provisions relating to the minimum balance requirement and waiting period for withdrawal, with a view to safeguarding the long-term social security interests of EPF members," the retirement fund body stated.Under SWP, retiring members can withdraw their accumulated PF savings at regular intervals, such as monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, based on their preference. Subscribers will also have the option to stop SWP whenever they want, apart from partial lumpsum withdrawal or only withdrawing the interest earned.The SWP facility would be entirely voluntary, thus ensuring stable post-retirement income, reducing reinvestment risks and strengthening fund sustainability. The minimum waiting period for making withdrawals under Employee Pension Scheme (EPS), however, remains unchanged at 36 months.Around 6.3 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years with provident fund accumulations of over Rs 5 lakh are expected to be primary beneficiaries of the proposed SWP framework. In case of the member's death during the payout period, a nominee or dependant will be able to withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments.TOIreported about this in a frontpage report Thursday.Vineet Nahata, MD, Power Gilt Treasuries, and member of Central Board of Trustees, said members will now get completely secure fixed income investment avenue with attractive interest earning, that too tax exempt till Rs 2.5 lakh annually. "It is a superior investment alternative compared to bank fixed deposits and mutual funds which are prone to credit risk and market fluctuations," he said.Additionally, in a move towards achieving universal social security, EPFO approved the introduction of a UAN-linked mechanism for direct voluntary contributions and third-party micro-contributions (such as customer tips), completely independent of traditional employer payroll systems. This will help people in the unorganised sector to accumulate their own PF savings, independent of any employer contributions.With a view to diversifying EPFO's investment portfolio and generate higher returns for its 30 crore members, the social security organisation also decided to permit investments up to 3% of its fresh annual accretions in eligible alternative investment funds. It can invest up to 5% of its fresh annual accretions in asset-backed and trust-structured investments, according to its pattern of investment. Initially, the plan is to channel worker capital through institutional giants such as National Investment and Infrastructure Fund and Sidbi's Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0.CBT also reviewed proposals for 27 establishments to surrender their EPF exemptions status and four establishments to have their exemption cancelled, transferring corpus of around Rs 6,000 crore, covering 1.5 lakh members, to EPFO's direct administration. Exempted establishments manage PFs on their own in accord with EPFO norms.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Expect more coordination among regulators: RBI deputy governor SC Murmu
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI deputy governor SC Murmu has called attention to overlapping regulatory jurisdictions in India's financial sector, pointing to related-party
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI deputy governor SC Murmu has called attention to overlapping regulatory jurisdictions in India's financial sector, pointing to related-party transactions, mis-selling of insurance and mutual fund products, and cybersecurity as areas requiring coordination among regulators.Speaking at the Gatekeepers of Governance 2026 event in Mumbai, Murmu said the mandates of financial regulators intersected in several areas, requiring greater coordination to address risks that cut across institutions and markets.A listed bank, for instance, is subject to RBI's prudential norms and related-party lending guidelines as well as listing regulations governing related-party transactions. "As regulators, our mandates intersect at many points," he said.The distribution of insurance and mutual fund products by banks is another area of overlap, with mis-selling falling within the jurisdiction of multiple regulators. "Banks distribute insurance and mutual funds, so mis-selling concerns all three regulators," he said.Cybersecurity presents a similar challenge because an incident at one institution can affect entities overseen by different regulators. Murmu said regulators needed to establish common standards for cyber resilience. "A single incident can hit a bank, an insurer, and a market infrastructure institution at once," he said.He said coordination among regulators would be necessary to address these overlapping responsibilities. "You can expect closer coordination among us," he said. Murmu also said regulation needed to focus on clearly communicating expectations rather than attempting to keep pace with every new development through additional rules.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: New Air India CEO briefs Noel, Chandra at Gurugram HQ
articles.summary: MUMBAI/NEW DELHI: Months after Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts and a director of Tata Sons, questioned the financial performance of Air India, he
articles.body: MUMBAI/NEW DELHI: Months after Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts and a director of Tata Sons, questioned the financial performance of Air India, he joined fellow Tata Sons directors on a visit to the airline's Gurugram headquarters and training academy on Thursday.The visit, organised by Tata Sons and Air India chairman N Chandrasekaran, was part of a broader effort to give directors deeper insight into the airline's operations, transformation programme and turnaround progress. Trusts vice-chairman and Tata Sons director Venu Srinivasan was the only absentee and is learnt to be in Botswana.Air India's new chief executive, Tewolde Gebremariam outlined the airline's roadmap to profitability, including plans to improve efficiencies, strengthen cost controls and drive greater synergies with Air India Express. Tata Sons directors also visited the airline's operations control centre, housed within the Gurugram campus. The visit came a day ahead of Air India's board meeting on Friday and followed hours of interactions between directors and the airline's senior management team.Air India has drawn scrutiny from Noel over losses and capital allocation. At Tata Sons' Feb board meeting, Noel raised concerns over the performance of Air India and other newer ventures, leading to the deferment of Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman.On Nov 14, Noel said he did not question "the direction" of Tata Sons' investments but questioned "the delivery" of those initiatives. Following the Feb board meeting, Chandrasekaran initiated a process under which heads of Air India, Tata Digital and Tata Electronics would present their financial and operational plans directly to the Tata Sons board.He also proposed visits by directors to Air India's Gurugram headquarters, Tata Electronics' semiconductor project at Dholera and Tata Digital's fulfillment and dark-store operations. Former Air India CEO Campbell Wilson, Tata Digital CEO Sajith Sivanandan and Tata Electronics CEO Randhir Thakur subsequently briefed directors on their businesses at Tata Sons board meeting in May. Thursday's visit to Air India's Gurugram facility marks the first board-level operational review under the initiative.Earlier this month, Tewolde said Air India has "punched below its weight" for too long and is mulling a fresh order for more wide body aircraft to "regain market share from competition (foreign airlines)" as that "business belongs to Air India." While the "short term" poses multiple "challenges", the "long term is a huge opportunity" and the airline could be profitable "very soon" by focusing on cutting costs and boosting revenue and efficiency, he said on Nov 3.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: MUMBAI: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, India's largest public philanthropic foundation and the principal shareholder in Tata Sons, will meet on Friday to consider grants and ongoing social programmes, with one proposal likely to attract attention: a Rs 50-crore funding package for Pune's Jehangir Hospital.The hospital is chaired by Jehangir H C Jehangir (73), a scion of the Cawasji family, who also serves as a trustee of the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, the second-largest shareholder in Tata Sons.The funding proposal found its way onto SDTT's board agenda after informal enquiries with the Tata Education and Development Trust (TEDT), failed to elicit support, said people familiar with the matter.The proposal is expected to secure approval, requiring the support of a majority of trustees. SDTT chairman Noel Tata, along with trustees Neville Tata and Bhaskar Bhat, is expected to back the proposal, the people said. The position of fellow trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh remains unclear ahead of Friday's board meeting.Jehangir had told TOI that he intends to expand the hospital's 350-bed capacity and its wellness centres. The expansion would be funded through internal accruals and other sources, while ruling out private equity funding, he had said. The proposal requires the SDTT board's consideration because grants exceeding Rs 15 crore cannot be approved through a circular resolution, a route available only for grants of up to Rs 15 crore.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Sarvam's Token Factory raises control issue
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Sarvam AI's Token Factory has allowed businesses to use China's DeepSeek and have their requests processed in India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sarvam AI's Token Factory has allowed businesses to use China's DeepSeek and have their requests processed in India. Running DeepSeek alongside its own model on Indian servers raises a question over India's push for sovereign AI. How much control does local hosting give businesses over models trained overseas?Token Factory connects a company's software to several AI models through a single interface, known as an API. Businesses can choose which model handles each request. Sarvam offers own 105B model alongside China's DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, and Google's Gemma. The company says it runs the models on clusters of graphics processors in India and matches or beats leading global providers on speed and cost for most of models it offers.Atul Arya, founder and CEO of AI services firm Blackstraw, said a model's country of origin deserves scrutiny, particularly from banks and insurers. Businesses should ask whether they can audit and secure the model, control how their data passes through it and understand where it falls short. "If I'm honest, a model from a 'trusted' country that you can't inspect or govern isn't much safer either," Arya said, adding, running a model in India can help regulated businesses address data security and compliance requirements."DeepSeek's Chinese origin is important, but less important than control." said Jaspreet Bindra, co-founder and CEO of AI & Beyond. In DeepSeek's case, he said, the test is whether Sarvam can independently inspect and secure the model, control its updates, set limits on its behaviour and keep critical functions running without relying on a foreign provider.Those capabilities would sit with Sarvam, and customers would still need to know whether their prompts and responses are retained or used for training, who can access the logs and what happens if a model is withdrawn. "Even if the provider has control over fine-tuning, patching and decommissioning the model, customers are still reliant on a third party," said Rajesh Chhabra, GM for India and Asia at cybersecurity firm Acronis.Queries sent to Sarvam remained unanswered.A single interface makes it easier to pick a model for each task, said Manik Nangia, chief business officer at Leadsquared, an AI-powered automation platform.Money habits form by age 7.
